newsitem.title: UK: Oil stocks rise on crude price surge. [CORRECTED 01:02 GMT 08/01]
newsitem.headline: Oil stocks rise on crude price surge. [CORRECTED 01:02 GMT 08/01]

text.p: Shares in Enterprise Oil led others in the sector higher on Tuesday as continuing cold weather across Europe and the U.S. helped to drive crude oil prices higher.
The shares were 11p higher at 646p by 0848 GMT. Lasmo was up 6-1/2p at 232p and British Borneo put on 7-1/2p to 812p.
IPE Brent crude futures surged on Monday amid forecasts for colder weather. The Brent February crude future trading on SIMEX was quoted at $24.50/$24.73 per barrel by 0437 GMT.

Brokers said they expected prices to remain supported by the severe winter weather in Europe and forecasts of below average temperatures in the U.S. Northeast, the largest heating oil market in the world.
Some brokers expected Brent crude to target its post-Gulf War high of $25.06 (corrects from $26.80) a barrel. February Brent closed 45 cents higher at $24.57 a barrel on Monday.

Traders said oil stocks were also benefiting from news of tightening supply, prompted by the weather. Iraq said it will reduce its crude exports, citing worries that high prices might mean it would overshoot its sales limit of $1 billion over three months under its "oil-for-food" deal with the United Nations.
Shares in other oil majors were also stronger. British Petroleum gained 6p to 688p whilst Shell added 2p to 10.07 stg.
